s1-core.summaryMarkdown: Full review at plan revision 5 (the stored review was cleared by the repair batch and CORE-2/CORE-3 changed, so no reattest). CORE-1: one `ServiceKey` space; runtime and type keys share descriptors, caches, resolution guards, scope and disposal paths; factory errors are not cached; typed behavior unchanged apart from a poisoned-lock or wrong-API resolve now naming its cause instead of `Missing`. CORE-2: thread-bound slots without `unsafe`; a wrong-thread resolve fails before touching the table; values are never dropped off their thread (drains run outside the `RefCell` borrow, the table drops with its thread); the API kind is checked before any factory runs or cached value is returned. CORE-3: factories are made (bounded by the default timeout under a timer) before ordering over both key kinds; per-service timeouts, concurrent layers, failures and timeouts all named. CORE-4: registration-key defaulting for every `add_startup_*` form, explicit keys kept. The four test groups prove each, including the new factory-timeout and wrong-API tests; my scratch probe confirmed the three repairs. The earlier findings f1-f3 are resolved. Residual, non-blocking: a scope whose descriptor snapshot predates the root re-registering a key as the other kind can read that kind's cached singleton as an opaque value (never the thread-bound value).

s2-theme.summaryMarkdown:
Passed. All five findings of the first review are resolved. I inspected the repair delta:

- `theme_keys_view::a_bound_text_style_follows_its_tokens`: a `bind_text_style(text, text_style_keys!(typography::h3))` node shows desktop's h3 and then, on the same node, touch's after `Density::Touch.set()`, with desktop != touch asserted first.
- The appearance test now binds `surfaces::APP` and asserts that Light != Dark before switching. Brand and Reset act on `APP`.
- `FixtureCommands` runs on the fixture only. `check` exits 1 for a missing file, `write` 0, `check` 0, and `check` 1 after one value is edited. A density token aliasing the accent color raises a `CodegenError` naming `borders-tint`, and `write` exits 2.
- `document()` now derives each token's owning modifier from `ROOTS` and stops on strays.
- `theming.md:211`, components `knowledge.md` and `SKILL.md:131-135` are corrected.

I reran the Python group (15 OK). `theme_codegen.py check` still reports `theme.json` current. The Rust groups' fresh passing results come from `check` at revision 39.

The first review's assessment of NSH-1 and THEME-1..4 stands: the pin, no old-theme API, no modifier set by RayX, Light/Dark outside the modifiers, Button token-for-token unchanged, and the document equal to the old dump in all 24 combinations.

s2-nsh-layer.summaryMarkdown: BLD-1..4 and RES-1..2 are met. Every TS builder method delegates to the Rust extension of its name, now including the options callback of `addApplicationConfiguration`. Options replay after binding and throw at the call. A single `start_app_with` serves Rust and TS roots, and `start` takes the builder in the JS call. The provider resolves by class or token, with `null` or an error naming the token, scopes, and disposal that deactivates view models. Listener members return NSH's `Stop`, so a consumer of a shared per-provider wrapper stops its own listeners. The old API is gone, and the moved groups keep their assertions. All four earlier findings are resolved. 8/8 sprint checks passed at revision 66, executed fresh. Accepted deviations: `ServiceKeyArg`/`Resolved` with typed `#[ts]` signatures; per-VM `sys.locals` tables keyed by the root's `Configuration`; the early `ServiceToken<T>`; `add_storage()` preferring `PlatformKeyValueStore`; lifecycle members on `SuspensionService`; builder methods returning `RayXAppBuilder`; per-provider wrapper identity, to be reconciled with TSS-1 in s3. CLI templates, gallery and docs belong to s4. Residual, not blocking: release when the reactive owner goes relies on NSH's `Stop` and is not exercised in RayX's tests; `merge` ignores unknown keys silently.

findings.descriptionMarkdown: Resolved: under `initialize_with_timer` each startup factory races the registry's default timeout; expiry fails startup as `timed_out` under the registration key with the display name.
Resolved: registrations record `thread_bound`, and `resolve_erased` refuses a resolve through the other API before any factory runs or a cached value is returned, typed and keyed.
Resolved: the docs now say orphans are released at the owning thread's next thread-bound resolve (table access) or by `release_orphaned_thread_bound_services`, matching the code.

**Expected:** t24 moves the old groups' still-valid assertions into the new groups, and THEME-2 requires that a key read in a binding follows a modifier change. The old `theme_view` group asserted that `bind_text_style` follows a density switch: font size, line height and letter spacing on the same view.

**Observed:** `bind_text_style` was rewritten onto `TextStyleKeys` (`crates/rayx_components/src/theme/mod.rs:305`, with the weight now an `untracked` snapshot), and `text_style_keys!` (`mod.rs:173`) is new. `theme_view` was deleted, and no test group calls either one: `grep -rn bind_text_style crates/rayx_components/tests examples/gallery/native` finds nothing. Only a `no_run` doctest compiles them. `Button` does not use them.

**Failure scenario:** a regression in `bind_text_style` passes every sprint check. For example, a binding that reads the keys outside its closure would freeze the text style after `Density::Touch.set()`. Yet `docs/components.md`, `theming.md` and `SKILL.md` all present it as the way to apply a text style.

**Repair:** add a case to `theme_keys_view` or `theme_modifiers_view`: a `bind_text_style(text(..), text_style_keys!(keys::platform::density::typography::h3))` view whose `text_styles` change from Desktop's to Touch's h3 values on the same node after `Density::Touch.set()`, with the expected values written as literals (as `button_view` does).

**Expected:** t23 asks the new group to test `check` on a stale document *on a small fixture export*, so that THEME-1's "`check` exits 1 when the committed document is not what the export generates" is proven wherever the group runs.

**Observed:** the only `check` test (`.claude/skills/rayx-components/scripts/test_theme_document.py:214-223`, `Commands`) uses the real export, and is skipped when `RayX.Design` is not beside RayX.Root. The fixture classes never call `main`, though `main` already takes `--tokens` and `--out`. I confirmed by hand that `check` exits 1 for an edited copy and for a missing file.

**Failure scenario:** in a checkout or CI run without RayX.Design, `c-theme-codegen` passes (the fixture tests satisfy `minimumTests`), even if `check` were broken to always exit 0.

**Repair:** in `FixtureExport`, write the fixture's `generate(self.dir)` to a temp file. Assert that `main(['check','--tokens',dir,'--out',stale])` returns 1 for a changed file and for a missing one, and that `write` followed by `check` returns 0.

**Expected:** `theming.md:211` says "`ROOTS` says which modifier picks each collection's values", and THEME-1 requires each context to override exactly the tokens its mode changes.

**Observed:** the modifier column of `ROOTS` (`.claude/skills/rayx-components/scripts/theme_codegen.py:56-61`) is never read: `declared` iterates `for root, _ in ROOTS` (`:315`). Instead, `document` (`:390-399`) diffs every token against the base for every modifier, with the other modifiers at their defaults. Today's export has no token that two modifiers change (I checked: the overlap is 0), so the output is correct. The implementer's 24-combination comparison confirms this, and I reran it: 0 differences.

**Failure scenario:** a future export with a `platform.density` token aliasing an accent color would get that token into both the `accent` and `density` contexts. NSH's later-modifier-wins rule (`theme_modifiers.rs` `tokens()`) would then draw `(sky, touch)` with the density context's value, which was computed at cyan. The generator would write it silently, and only `theme_modifiers_view::each_context_changes_only_tokens_of_its_collections` would catch it after the fact.

**Repair:** either use `ROOTS`' modifier column, so that `document` raises `CodegenError` when a context changes a token outside its collections (with a fixture test for that), or drop the column and correct `theming.md:211`.

**Expected:** `theme_keys_view::a_binding_follows_the_appearance_and_the_apps_tokens` proves that a document token read through a key follows Light/Dark.

**Observed:** it uses `roles-primary-bg`, which in the default (cyan) context is the same in Light and Dark (`cssVars.theme`: `#007796ff`). So `app.press("Dark"); app.wait(|s| bg(s) == Some(dark))` (`crates/rayx_components/tests/theme_keys_view.rs:110-114`) passes at once, before the appearance changes. The later `Brand` step does show that the appearance reached Dark, but only for an app-set color. The document case is covered elsewhere, for sky only, in `theme_modifiers_view::light_and_dark_follow_the_appearance_in_a_context`.

**Failure scenario:** if `TokenKey::get` stopped reading the appearance for document tokens, this step would still pass.

**Repair:** bind a token that differs between Light and Dark at the defaults (for example `surfaces::APP`, `#f5f5f5ff` / `#0a0a0aff`), and assert `light != dark` before pressing Dark.

**Expected:** THEME-4 requires the docs, the skill and memory to describe the document, the keys and the modifiers. No current knowledge may describe the removed system as live.

**Observed:**

- RayX `.agentx/memory/knowledge/components/knowledge.md:18-21` (status current) still explains that `RayXTheme`'s `AppTheme` is written by hand with roles in `roles.rs`.
- The same file's line 28 cites the deleted group `theme_tsx`.
- RayX.Root `.claude/skills/rayx-components/SKILL.md:131-134` says crates.io's NSH "lacks the theme API (`AppTheme`, `TokenSpec`, `nsh_base::role`)", but on `nshx-0.5.0-4` those names no longer exist, and what upstream lacks is theme documents and typed keys.

Neither static grep's pattern covers these names, and the RayX grep excludes `.agentx/`.

**Failure scenario:** a later session reads the `components` knowledge or SKILL.md, believes RayX still has a hand-written `AppTheme` and `roles.rs` (or that a missing `AppTheme` is the symptom to look for), and looks for or restores the removed system.

**Repair:** mark the `AppTheme`/`roles.rs` bullet historical or remove it (the role mapping now lives in `ROLE_TOKENS` in the generator), point the `leading`/`tracking` bullet at `theme_modifiers_tsx`, and reword SKILL.md:134 to name what crates.io's NSH lacks (theme documents, `theme_keys!`, modifiers).
Listener members return NSH's `Stop`, so each consumer of a shared wrapper stops its own listener; disposing the object still stops all of them. Proven by `nsh_tsx_listeners.rs`.
`start` is synchronous and returns `Later`, taking the builder in the JS call; a builder method in the same turn throws `BuilderStarted` and never reaches startup.
`a_start_on_a_ready_surface_keeps_its_root` starts again with `start()` and `start_async()` after `Ready` and shows the first root kept.
`addApplicationConfiguration(options => …)` records `name`, `description` and `merge` and replays them after binding. The test shows the override, the kept file value and a refused merge.
